title: Finance, Growth and Decay
summary: Simple and compound decay (straight-line and reducing-balance depreciation), nominal and effective interest rates, and timelines with changing rates, deposits and withdrawals.

notes.latex: A = P(1 + in) \qquad A = P(1 + i)^n
notes.caption: Simple and compound growth ($P$ principal, $A$ accumulated amount, $i$ interest rate as a decimal, $n$ number of periods)

rows: The value drops by the same amount every year
The value drops by the same percentage of the current value every year

notes.title: Worked example 1
notes.problem: A car bought for R250 000 depreciates at 15% p.a. Find its value after 4 years using (a) straight-line and (b) reducing-balance depreciation.

notes.title: Worked example 2: finding the rate
notes.problem: A machine bought for R80 000 is worth R45 000 after 5 years of reducing-balance depreciation. Find the annual rate.

notes.text: A **nominal** rate is the quoted annual rate, compounded $m$ times a year (e.g. 12% p.a. compounded monthly). The **effective** rate is the equivalent rate compounded once a year.

notes.caption: $m$ = number of compounding periods per year (monthly 12, quarterly 4, half-yearly 2)

notes.title: Worked example 3
notes.problem: Convert 9% p.a. compounded monthly to an effective annual rate.

notes.label: Exam tip
notes.text: When interest is compounded monthly, both $i$ and $n$ must be in months: $i = \frac{\text{annual rate}}{12}$ and $n = $ number of years $\times 12$.
When rates change, or money is added or withdrawn, draw a **timeline**. Move each amount forward to the end date at the correct rate for each period, then add (deposits) or subtract (withdrawals).

notes.title: Worked example 4
notes.problem: R10 000 is invested at 8% p.a. compounded annually. After 2 years the rate changes to 10% p.a. compounded annually. What is the investment worth after 5 years?

questions.prompt: A laptop costing R12 000 depreciates by 20% p.a. on the straight-line method. What is it worth after 3 years?
A tractor costing R400 000 depreciates at 12% p.a. on the reducing-balance method. Find its value after 6 years, to the nearest rand.
Convert 12% p.a. compounded quarterly to an effective annual rate, as a percentage correct to two decimal places.
For an investment over 4 years with interest compounded monthly, what is $n$?
R5 000 is invested at 7% p.a. compounded monthly for 3 years. Find the final amount, correct to the nearest cent.
For the same nominal rate, interest compounded monthly gives more than interest compounded annually.
A car worth R180 000 depreciates to R110 000 in 4 years on the reducing-balance method. Calculate the rate of depreciation.
R20 000 is invested at 9% p.a. compounded annually. After 3 years, R5 000 is withdrawn. What is the balance after 5 years?
An effective rate of 10% p.a. is required. What nominal rate, compounded monthly, gives this?
How many years will it take for an item to lose half its value at 15% p.a. reducing-balance depreciation? (Use trial and improvement or logs; give a whole number of years.)
